Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a right-sided lobulated soft-tissue mass in the superior mediastinum that aligns with the esophageal course; this radiographic appearance, combined with symptoms of dysphagia and dyspepsia, is most consistent with an esophageal lipoma. Other options like thymoma (anterior), neurogenic tumor (posterior), or calcified granuloma do not fit the specific location, morphology, or clinical presentation described.
